gloss: to tease, to make fun of; to window-shop

definitions.gloss: to tease, to make fun of, to jeer at
definitions.explanation: To mock or ridicule someone in a playful or slightly malicious way, often by making comments about their behavior or situation.

definitions.gloss: to window-shop, to browse without buying
definitions.explanation: To look at goods in a shop or stall without intending to purchase anything.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}を{冷|ひ}やかした。
{彼|かれ}がデートに{行|い}くと{言|い}ったら、みんなに{冷|ひ}やかされた。
examples.english: When he said he was going on a date, everyone teased him.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}を{冷|ひ}やかすのはやめなさい。
examples.english: Stop making fun of the newcomer.

examples.japanese: {店|みせ}を{冷|ひ}やかして{歩|ある}いた。
{買|か}うつもりはないが、{骨董品|こっとうひん}{店|てん}を{冷|ひ}やかしに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I had no intention of buying, but went to browse the antique shop.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{屋台|やたい}を{冷|ひ}やかしながら{友人|ゆうじん}と{楽|たの}しく{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: I had a good time with a friend browsing the festival stalls.

notes:
Originally related to {冷|ひ}やす (to cool), but the modern meanings have diverged.

TRANSITIVITY:
・Type: transitive ({他動詞|たどうし})
・Pattern: AがBを{冷|ひ}やかす (A teases B / A browses B)

ASPECT (ている):
・{冷|ひ}やかしている = is teasing / is browsing (ongoing action)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{人|ひと}を{冷|ひ}やかす (to tease someone)
・{店|みせ}を{冷|ひ}やかす (to browse a shop)
・{冷|ひ}やかされる (to be teased — passive)
・{冷|ひ}やかし{半分|はんぶん}に (half-jokingly)

USAGE NOTES:
The teasing sense (sense 1) is the more common usage today. The window-shopping sense (sense 2) is somewhat old-fashioned but still understood. The noun form {冷|ひ}やかし refers to either the act of teasing or of browsing without buying.
